summary: Ray-plane intersection. a2 is a plane (XYZ normal plus a2[3] plane-distance term), a3 is the ray origin, a4 the ray target. Computes dot products to form a denominator; returns NULL when the ray is parallel to the plane (denominator 0.0) or when the resulting t-value fails validation via ArithmeticComparison_a88f. Otherwise writes the interpolated intersection point O + t*(P-O) into a1 (three consecutive floats) and returns a1.

operations.description: Compute v4 = dot(plane normal a2, ray origin a3) = a2[0]*a3[0] + a2[1]*a3[1] + a2[2]*a3[2].
Compute denominator v5 = v4 - dot(plane normal a2, ray target a4) = v4 - (a2[0]*a4[0] + a2[2]*a4[2] + a2[1]*a4[1]).
If v5 == 0.0 (ray parallel to plane, zero denominator), return NULL (no intersection).
Compute t-value v7 = (v4 + a2[3]) / v5, combining the plane-distance term a2[3] with the dot products.
Call ArithmeticComparison_a88f on the computed t-value v7 to validate it.
If ArithmeticComparison_a88f returns false for v7, return NULL (t-value rejected).
Write intersection X to a1[0] = (a4[0] - a3[0]) * v7 + a3[0].
Write intersection Y to a1[1] = (a4[1] - a3[1]) * v7 + a3[1].
Write intersection Z to a1[2] = (a4[2] - a3[2]) * v7 + a3[2].
Return the intersection point pointer a1 on success, or NULL on the two rejection paths.
